مَخْرَجٌ an inf. n. of 1. (S, Msb, K.) ―
-b2- Also A place of خُرُوج [i. e. of going, coming, passing, or getting, out, or forth; a place of egress, or exit; an outlet]: (S, K, TA:) pl. مَخَارِجُ. (TA.) You say, وَجَدْتُ فِى الأَمْرِ مَخْرَجًا (assumed tropical:) I found, in the affair, or case, a place [or way] of escape, evasion, or safety. (Msb.) And فُلَانٌ يَعْرِفُ مَوَالِجَ الأُمُورِ وَمَخَارِجَهَا (tropical:) Such a one knows the ways of entering into affairs and those of withdrawing himself out of them. (A, TA.) ―
-b3- [Hence, A privy: used in this sense in the S and K in art. حش, &c. ―
-b4- And The anus: used in this sense in the Msb in art. حقن.] ―
-b5- Also A time of خُرُوج [i. e. of going, &c., out, or forth; of egress, or exit]. (TA.) ―
-b6- فُلَانٌ حَسَنُ المَدْخَلِ والمَخْرَجِ means (assumed tropical:) Such a one is good, and laudable, in his way of acting, or conduct. (TA in art. دخل.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
